sheets.title: The Atlas World — Mariners' Chart
sheets.note: The compiled world chart on the redrawn 400 x 400 km frame: 13 landmasses generated from one seed, 3 oceans, 9 marginal seas nested inside them, 47 settlement marks — one per f-town-* feature — and honest empty parchment everywhere the survey has never reached. Four of the thirteen are filled, because only reported ground takes ink here: two in the ice pattern (Rimewall Cap, the one true ice cap at composition ice 96.9, and Skerryfast, a chain that is 75% ice) and two in the hearsay hatch, the only reported density this world rolls a landmass up to. The other nine draw as a bare outline — no trunk node carries a `survey` field, so the chart claims only that they are not reported; towns fall on seven of the thirteen, Ashen Spar and Wracklow carry nothing, and Wealdmarch alone carries the sheet's two region bounds. All thirteen landmasses are lettered: thirty-two names asked, thirty-two placed, none dropped, against a thirty-two-label budget. The basin miniature, the drawn west coast and the Meltwash are NOT on this sheet — STATE §28 ruling 8 retired them from it; Task 8 re-draws that ground on its own continent sheet, which does not exist yet.

sheets.title: Target-Density Canary
sheets.note: NOT GEOGRAPHY — a synthetic sheet at the agreed target density (13 landmasses, 160 regions, 1,740 landform instances, 340 labels) on the atlas sheet's own 400 km frame. It exists so a render regression at scale is visible before the real world exists.

sheets.title: The Generated World — Fabric Survey
sheets.note: 13 landmasses, 160 regions, 47 settlements, 40 roads and 2 sea lanes drawn straight from content/world/fabric/ — the generated layer, before any authored meaning is joined on. The 40 surveyed regions are inked; the 120 reported ones are bare parchment, which is spec §6.4's honest-frontier gradient drawn rather than described. No names: naming is Plan D's.

sheets.title: Coastline Overlay — Baseline vs Generated
sheets.note: Baseline coastline ghosted under the generated one, with a per-continent area-delta table joined through the manifest's landmasses[].nodeId. Since the redraw the committed trunk IS drawn from this fabric, so the sheet reads as a near-identity rather than a before/after: 13 baseline polygons against 13 generated, gross land 65,498.4 → 65,599.5 km² (x1.00), every continent between x0.99 and x1.05, and sea:land 1.44 : 1 on the committed trunk, which is what G-SEALAND measures; the sheet's own footer line quotes the fabric layer's generated figure instead, and the two are different measures of the same world. Baseline read from the draft folder's baseline/ when one is present and from content/spine/nodes otherwise, never from git.
